title: Healthcare Analytics Professional Simulation
note: Formative assessment; not psychometrically validated or an employer credential.

assessments.title: Investigate an encounter extract
assessments.prompt: A monthly extract contains 1,000 rows. Checks find 12 duplicate encounter IDs, 8 missing department values, 5 discharge dates before admission, and 15 negative length-of-stay values. Some rows may have more than one issue. The dashboard total is 1,000. Specify the investigation sequence, quarantine policy, reconciliation, and what you would tell the operations lead.
rubric: Distinguishes row count from unique encounter count
Profiles each issue and checks overlap before summing
Defines rule-based accept/quarantine with reason codes
Reconciles raw = accepted + quarantined and records exclusions
Explains impact on denominator and dashboard caveat
assessments.model: Preserve an immutable raw copy and profile row count, key uniqueness, nulls, date order and LOS bounds. Investigate overlaps at row level: issue counts cannot be summed to estimate affected rows. Quarantine records failing critical rules with stable reason codes; do not silently delete or impute. Produce accepted and quarantine tables plus row-level audit log. Reconcile raw rows = accepted + quarantined and verify unique encounter IDs in accepted data. Recompute dashboard totals from accepted records, state the excluded count and issue mix, and obtain data-owner confirmation for ambiguous rules.

assessments.title: Interpret a bed occupancy change
assessments.prompt: A hospital reports 92% bed occupancy this month versus 84% last month. Available staffed bed-days fell from 3,000 to 2,500; occupied bed-days rose from 2,520 to 2,300? The report may contain inconsistent values. Identify the arithmetic issue, calculate the correct rates, and explain what should be checked before operational conclusions.
rubric: Checks numerator/denominator arithmetic
Calculates rates correctly
Flags inconsistent trend narrative
Checks staffed-bed definition and period comparability
Avoids causal or quality claims from occupancy alone
assessments.model: Last month: 2,520 / 3,000 = 84%. This month: 2,300 / 2,500 = 92%. Occupied bed-days actually decreased by 220 while available staffed bed-days decreased by 500; the occupancy rate rose because the denominator contracted faster. Confirm bed-day definitions, staffed versus licensed beds, closures, reporting period, and whether occupied bed-days include observation/overflow. Occupancy alone does not establish efficiency or quality.

assessments.title: Review a prescribing dashboard
assessments.prompt: A dashboard ranks departments by antihypertensive use. It shows raw prescription counts without patient or encounter denominators, combines inpatient and outpatient orders, includes discontinued orders, and has no date filter or missing-data indicator. List the critical defects and propose a safer redesign.
rubric: Identifies denominator and exposure mismatch
Separates care settings and order statuses
Defines valid time window and filters
Adds missingness/data freshness/context
Uses normalized rates and cautious interpretation
assessments.model: Do not rank departments using raw counts when patient volume differs. Separate inpatient and outpatient populations, define order grain, include only valid order statuses for the stated question, and distinguish orders from unique patients. Add a reporting period, department and setting filters, data freshness, missingness and exclusions. Consider orders per 100 encounters or proportion of eligible patients receiving therapy, with explicit denominator and confidence/context. Avoid implying appropriateness or effectiveness from utilization counts.

assessments.title: Specify a safe patient-level aggregation
assessments.prompt: An orders table has multiple medication orders per encounter and an encounters table has one row per encounter. A join followed by COUNT(*) is described as the number of patients treated. Explain why this may be wrong and provide a defensible SQL pattern for unique patients with at least one active antihypertensive order.
rubric: Recognizes one-to-many join multiplication
Uses explicit active-order filter
Counts distinct patient identifiers
Defines drug-class mapping source
Checks unmatched keys and date window
assessments.model: COUNT(*) counts joined order rows, not patients. Use COUNT(DISTINCT e.patient_id) after joining on encounter_id and filtering order_status = 'Active', the defined antihypertensive drug-class mapping, and the requested date window. Confirm patient_id is populated and stable, inspect unmatched encounter IDs, and document whether the cohort is encounter-based or patient-based. See the runnable SQLite reference query in sql/reference_queries.sql.
